function: Prompt-based LLM optimizer jointly decides task offloading and uplink power per sub-channel from IoT terminals to LEO satellites to minimize average latency (p. 4).
system: N=5-20 IoT terminals (gain 3 dBi) uplink to M=3-6 LEO satellites at 550 km; I=4-8 sub-channels of 10 MHz; 3.49 GHz; no RIS (p. 3, 6-7).
method: Pretrained GPT-4o queried through its API, no dedicated training: prompts, example pool and expert/reminder prompts drive iterations; Lagrange closed form for satellite computing; alternating optimization (p. 4-5).
data_channel: Simulated channel: free-space path loss with Rician fading (factor K) and LEO elevation geometry; uniform random task sizes 0.3-0.6 MB; no training dataset (p. 3, 6).
test_conditions: No model training. Each scenario solved by its own prompting run: N=5-20, M=3-6, I=4-8, 10 runs; temperature and prompt wording examined at N=10, M=3, I=4 (p. 6-7).
baselines: Non-learned: genetic algorithm, random choice, processing all locally. Learned: DDPG with three-layer actor and critic, learning rate 1e-5, exploration rate 0.05 (p. 6).
metrics: Average latency of IoT terminals in ms (mean and standard deviation over 10 runs) and iterations to convergence versus GA and DDPG (p. 6-7).
complexity: None; only 40 to 200 iterations to converge are reported, and LLM response time is left as future work (p. 6-7).
openness: None; no code or data link, GPT-4o accessed through a commercial API (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 3: "represents the Rician fading with factor K" - custom channel of free-space path loss and Rician fading (Table I, p. 6); no 3GPP TR 38.811 model or measured data is stated.
q2_support: p. 2: "avoiding the costs of dedicated model training" - nothing is trained; the LLM is prompted for each scenario, and Figs. 4-5 (p. 6-7) only vary N, M and I, although the abstract claims "generalization capability across scenarios with varying numbers of satellites and IoT" terminals.
q3_support: p. 6: "the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient" (learned DDPG) plus GA, random choice and all-local (non-learned) are compared on mean latency; p. 6: "the proposed LLM-based algorithm achieves the lowest mean latency".
q4_support: p. 7: "such as the response time of LLMs" is left as future work; only convergence in 40 to 200 iterations (p. 6) is reported, with no complexity order, operations, parameters or runtime.
q5_support: p. 5: "commercial APIs for performance evaluation" - GPT-4o is used through a commercial API; the channel is a custom simulation (Table I, p. 6) and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included as area 6: the LLM learns a physical-layer decision (uplink power on satellite links) jointly with task offloading, so it passes above_phy; the satellite CPU allocation is a closed form (p. 4). The pretrained LLM is used through prompts without task training; treated as the learned component, reviewer to confirm. q2 is borderline: the abstract claims generalization across numbers of satellites and terminals (p. 2) and Figs. 4-5 vary N, M, I, but nothing is trained; marked 0. The LLM is outperformed by GA in three of five scenarios of Fig. 5 (p. 7). The PDF is the accepted version; p. 1 is a repository cover page showing DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3612207, which matches. The terminal model has only an antenna gain, no array.
